ledger.note: c. 1600: the Tai alliance of the north-west. The page says 'the alliance has been formalized since at least the 17th century' and the infobox 'Established: before 17th century'; Tai peoples settled the north-west 'since the early first millennium CE or, at the latest, the fifth to eighth century'. 1600 is a placeholder for 'before the 17th century'.

July 1948: the Tai Federation. 'An accord was finally promulgated in July 1948, creating an independent Tai Federation in the Union française' with its capital at Muang Lay; it was made a crown domain of Emperor Bao Dai in 1950. Before 1948 the infobox holds 'French protectorate, part of Tonkin, French Indochina (1889-1948)': Pavie signed a protectorate treaty with Deo Van Tri on 7 April 1889.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; named by se-01-i (Luang Prabang's tributary 'Sip Song Chau Tai' 1707-1889). Two pages, both thin: neither gives an area, a canton list or a pre-1886 date, so the 1600 start and the three-province shape are confidence-1 readings. Not settled: (1) the overlordships ('At different times, it had to pay tribute to China, Vietnam, Lan Xang/Luang Phrabang' and/or Siam; the 1779 and 1830s Siamese dates and the 1870s Haw invasions are not on the pages) belong to those states' dossiers; (2) the French protectorate of 1889-1948 (treaty 7 April 1889 per the Sip Song Chau Tai page, not found on the Deo Van Tri page) is for french-indochina to carry as a vassal pair; (3) a Tai polity would not normally have 'capital: none' for three centuries; (4) the infobox calls the dissolution 1954 and the successor 'North Vietnam', which is the democratic-republic-of-vietnam row (Cliopatria 1956-1975).
